developmentProcess.content: Chemex is an LLM-based product attributes system. It has two distinct components: a smaller model that will infer the groups and types of features to extract for a given category of products across a language. Then there is a much larger model doing the inference of those features for a given product. I was mainly part of the development of the first part, while supporting the larger bulk inference infrastructure.

developmentProcess.title: Development
items: Helped lead an small internal team of engineers to design and implement this
Experimented with new prompt-tuning techniques to improve LLM accuracy and different parameters (Top-P + Top-K) and inputs to help with consistency among runs.
Worked with cross-functional teams to determine the criteria of good attribute coverage for different features.

developmentProcess.title: Technical Challenges Solved:
items: Better handles ambiguous or incomplete product data that we previously ignored.
Can rename/restrict attributes easily for specific Google features (make sure they are below a certain amount of characters or ensuring they do not include brand specific features).
Faster creation of product attributes at scale using LLMs, reducing time to live from 2 weeks of manual processing to just a few days.
Fast override mechanism for incorrect attributes identified by users or internal teams. Before we had to hide/remove the entire attribute, now we can fix just the incorrect part.

developmentProcess.title: Impact:
developmentProcess.content: The system is now live in some areas of Google Search, improving attribute coverage and helping users better determine product relevance on their "Shopping Journey". Coverage increased by +20% in the launched categories and english locales, leading to other features having an easier launch path.
